title: umbra
description: kate banazi and ryan mcgoldrick of rye. were introduced through localdesign. the two have similar ideologies on re-use, distortion and the manipulation of substrate and light and decided to work together to create an item that will be shown during milan design week 2017. the concept of the piece was to create a collaboration of two halves, where the juxtaposition of two practices and personalities meet whilst not compromising our individual voices. the aluminium light shades were hand spun in mittagong and hand finished at the workshop facilities in the university of canberra. they were then given their anodised finish by the team at f!nk design in queanbeyan.

honest.made in: spun in mittagong, finished at the university of canberra, anodised by f!nk design in queanbeyan

detail.note: the aluminium shades were hand spun in mittagong.

title: kleingeld
description: Produced in either brass or aluminium the material selections are weighty and cool to the touch, the tactile feedback one experiences with metals has an innate value that subtly increases engagement and awareness of the present interaction. To remove coins that you need for the morning/day/evening you need to carefully extract them, the design features uncomfortably sharp lines to the touch, not harmful however if you are hasty in removing coins it is likely to be uncomfortable. Currently only produced for the Australian currency, other currencies can be made to order.

title: maltmade
description: MaltMade is a concept and proof of concept exploring what coasters within a commercial hospitality environment could be like, it looks to an alternative material perhaps better suited to disposability. malt roots, the material that is a by-product from the malting industry which this project is exploring the use of, are super absorbent and a natural fertiliser, which mean not only can they function as a coaster but they are actually good for the evironment when they are disposed of, and re-use what is already inter-industry waste to create a potential second income stream for pelleting manufacturers by making minor changes to the current infrastructure. the maltmade coasters when disposed act as a nutrious mulch, helping keep moisture in the soil, and when over time they breakdown provide substantial nutriants to the soil/compost.

specs.course: design a sustainable value chain, bauhaus exchange
specs.material: pelleted malt rootlets, guar / water binder

title: heritage extension dining table
description: designed for king living the heritage extension dining table is a generous 6-10 seater extending dining table with a 1000mm extension (2.4m-3.4m). the design of the table features patent pending King SoftTouch Technology ® which was developed for this table. beyond the effortless assisted opening and closing the table features a unique steel frame that extends from the table top coupled through to the legs all the way to the floor. the table also smartly uses raw material resources with plywood making the core of the table design paired with thick american hardwood veneers. designed to last generations of dining moments. the table is also available as a 2.4m fixed version.
credit: Designed in my role as Industrial Designer at King Living, 2022–present. © King Living.

honest.made of: plywood core with thick american hardwood veneers, steel frame

detail.note: patent pending king softtouch technology® assists opening and closing.

title: hullbot autonomous robot
description: Working with the team at Hullbot in their Sydney Office, Building the world’s most sophisticated underwater drone. Working as one of two industrial designers alongside a small team of electrical, software and mechanical engineers designed from the ground up to autonomously inspect, map and clean the hull of a boat without a human operator present. Hullbot stops the growth of marine organisms, improving performance and extending time between haul-outs. Since moving on from working with the team on the design and hardware I have assisted with generating visualisation assets.
credit: Designed in my role as Industrial Designer at Hullbot, 2017–2019. © Hullbot.

title: universal thread adapter kit
description: Designed with the team at RØDE at their design and manufacturing facility in Sydney, Australia. The Thread Adaptor is a premium universal adaptor kit for mounting a range of devices onto any mic stand, boompole, tripod or studio arm. It features 1/4, 3/8, and 5/8 inch adaptors in a unique integrated set with a carabiner for safekeeping. These can be configured to connect any standard thread to any standard mount – a lifesaver on set, in the studio, or in the field – and it features a handy driver for tightening and loosening the adaptors. The Thread Adaptor features a bespoke design with a premium feel and finish – a must-have "everyday carry" accessory for sound engineers, filmmakers, and photographers.
credit: Designed in my role as Industrial Designer at RØDE, 2020–2022. © RØDE Microphones.
